offlineFirstStartSubstitution.loadBearingAssumptionVerified: The substitution only holds if the denial is inherited by the candidate's children -- notably the omega-effectd engine. This reviewer verified inheritance empirically to two levels: sandboxed sh -> curl and sandboxed sh -> sh -> curl are both denied, while the same shell unsandboxed returns 200.
offlineFirstStartSubstitution.onTheDecision: Declining to take the host network down while another lane was driving an unattended run was the correct call. Damaging a concurrent run to obtain a marginally broader control would have been the wrong trade.
offlineFirstStartSubstitution.question: Is per-process network denial equivalent to an offline first start, or is it weaker?
offlineFirstStartSubstitution.reviewerReproduction: Reproduced independently and strengthened. Under a (deny network*) sandbox profile, curl to zed.dev and to github.com both fail; unsandboxed, BOTH github.com and zed.dev return 200 inside the same two-second window.
offlineFirstStartSubstitution.strongerThanTheProducersOwnControl: The producer showed only github.com reachable unsandboxed. This reviewer also showed ZED.DEV reachable unsandboxed (200). That is the control that matters: it proves zed.dev was reachable from this host at review time, so 'no request reached zed.dev' is a property of the product and not an artifact of an unreachable host.
offlineFirstStartSubstitution.theOneResidual: Per-process denial does not exclude an UNSANDBOXED helper already running on the host relaying network-derived data to the candidate over IPC. A host outage would exclude that. The residual is small -- the engine child is spawned by the sandboxed parent and inherits the denial -- but it is the one respect in which the substitution is genuinely weaker, and it should be stated rather than glossed.
offlineFirstStartSubstitution.verdict: MATERIALLY EQUIVALENT for the property under test, and STRONGER in one respect, with one named residual. This reviewer accepts it.
offlineFirstStartSubstitution.whyStronger: It proves the property for the process under test rather than for the machine, and it isolates the result from anything else running on the host.

zedIsolationMethodAssessment.question: Is the replacement for the unsound whole-tree digest adequate?
zedIsolationMethodAssessment.rankingTheThreeOracles: The descriptor oracle is the strongest of the three, because it is a capability observation rather than a sampling one: a process that never opened a Zed path cannot have modified one. The path-set and per-file oracles are sampling observations and cannot exclude a write made and reverted inside the window. That residual is worth naming, and the descriptor result covers it.
zedIsolationMethodAssessment.reviewerContribution: Reproduced the descriptor oracle on the owner's live rc18 (0 zed / 14 omega / 123 total; engine child 0 zed / 4 omega) and added the missing live positive control (running Zed pid 77676 holds 52 zed paths).
zedIsolationMethodAssessment.verdict: SOUND, and materially better than what it replaces.
zedIsolationMethodAssessment.why: The whole-tree digest failed for a stated and correct reason -- Zed writes its own database log while running, so the tree drifts independently of the candidate. The replacement attacks exactly that: a used-path set, a controlled per-file diff, and a 90-second zero-drift control window that makes 'zero changed' a result rather than a too-short sample. Recording the control window is the part that makes it honest.
